problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), Z.dvd ((Z.fact x0 * Z.fact x1) * Z.fact (x0 + x1)) (Z.fact (N.double x0) * Z.fact (N.double x1))

problems.name: imo1978_p1
problems.text: Let m and n be natural numbers with 1 <= m < n. The last three digits of 1978^m are the same as the last three digits of 1978^n. Find m and n for which m + n is as small as possible.
problems.notes: "the last three digits agree" is 1000 | 1978^n - 1978^m. The statement says that every such pair has m + n >= 106, and that (3, 103) is a pair (m + n = 106)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), Npos XH <= x0 -> x0 < x1 -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))) ^ x1 - Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))) ^ x0) -> Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO (XI XH))))))) <= Z.of_N x0 + Z.of_N x1 /\ Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))) ^ Npos (XI (XI (XI (XO (XO (XI XH)))))) - Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))) ^ Npos (XI XH))

problems.name: imo1982_p4a
problems.text: Prove that if a positive integer n can be written as n = x^3 - 3 x y^2 + y^3 with integers x and y, then it has at least three such representations (three different pairs (x, y)).
problems.notes: the pairs (x, y), (y - x, -x), (-y, x - y) all represent n, and they are pairwise different when n > 0 (a repeated pair would be a fixed point of the map (x, y) -> (y - x, -x), whose only fixed point is the origin)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> (x0 ^ Npos (XI XH) - (Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) * x0) * x1 ^ Npos (XO XH)) + x1 ^ Npos (XI XH) = x2 -> ((x1 - x0) ^ Npos (XI XH) - (Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) * (x1 - x0)) * Z.neg x0 ^ Npos (XO XH)) + Z.neg x0 ^ Npos (XI XH) = x2 /\ ((Z.neg x1 ^ Npos (XI XH) - (Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) * Z.neg x1) * (x0 - x1) ^ Npos (XO XH)) + (x0 - x1) ^ Npos (XI XH) = x2 /\ (Not (x0 = x1 - x0 /\ x1 = Z.neg x0) /\ (Not (x0 = Z.neg x1 /\ x1 = x0 - x1) /\ Not (x1 - x0 = Z.neg x1 /\ Z.neg x0 = x0 - x1))))

problems.name: imo1982_p4b
problems.text: Show that the equation x^3 - 3 x y^2 + y^3 = 2891 has no solution in integers x, y.
problems.notes: no integer pair gives 2891 in the box and in the range checked by imo_truth.py (|x|, |y| <= 400); the proof is a computation modulo 9
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Not ((x0 ^ Npos (XI XH) - (Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) * x0) * x1 ^ Npos (XO XH)) + x1 ^ Npos (XI XH) = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XO (XI (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI (XO XH)))))))))))))

problems.name: imo1984_p6
problems.text: Let a, b, c, d be odd positive integers with a < b < c < d and ad = bc. Suppose that a + d = 2^k and b + c = 2^m for some integers k and m. Prove that a = 1.
problems.notes: the odd numbers are written a = 2x + 1, b = 2y + 1, c = 2z + 1, d = 2t + 1 with x, y, z, t >= 0 (so a < b is x < y, and a = 1 is x = 0); a + d = 2x + 2t + 2 and b + c = 2y + 2z + 2
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), forall (x4 : N), forall (x5 : N), Z.zero <= x0 -> x0 < x1 -> x1 < x2 -> x2 < x3 -> (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) * (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x3 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) = (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x1 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) * (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x2 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) -> (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0 + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x3) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) = Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x4 -> (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x1 + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x2) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) = Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x5 -> x0 = Z.zero

problems.name: imo1996_p4
problems.text: The positive integers a and b are such that the numbers 15a + 16b and 16a - 15b are both squares of positive integers. What is the least possible value of the smaller of these two squares?
problems.notes: the two squares are r^2 and s^2; the statement says that r and s are both at least 481 (so the smaller square is at least 481^2), and that a = 14911, b = 481 make both squares equal to 481^2
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> Z.zero < x2 -> Z.zero < x3 -> Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XI XH)))) * x0 + Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO XH))))) * x1 = x2 * x2 -> Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO XH))))) * x0 - Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XI XH)))) * x1 = x3 * x3 -> Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))) <= x2 /\ (Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))) <= x3 /\ (Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XI XH)))) * Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XI (XI (XI (XI (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI XH)))))))))))))) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO XH))))) * Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))) = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))) * Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))) /\ Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO XH))))) * Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XI (XI (XI (XI (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XI XH)))))))))))))) - Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XI XH)))) * Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))) = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))) * Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH)))))))))))

problems.name: imo1989_p5
problems.text: Prove that for each positive integer n there exist n consecutive positive integers none of which is a prime or a prime power.
problems.notes: "neither a prime nor a prime power" for a number m + i >= 2 means that it has two different prime divisors, i.e. it is a product a b of two coprime numbers a, b > 1. The test range is n <= 3 (the first three consecutive numbers of this kind are 20, 21, 22); imo_truth.py finds them for every n <= 7
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Ex Z (fun (x2 : Z) => Z.zero < x2 /\ (forall (x3 : Z), Z.of_N (Npos XH) <= x3 /\ x3 <= x0 -> Ex Z (fun (x5 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x6 : Z) => Z.of_N (Npos XH) < x5 /\ (Z.of_N (Npos XH) < x6 /\ (Z.coprime x5 x6 /\ x5 * x6 = x2 + x3))))))

problems.name: imo2012_p4
problems.text: Find all functions f from the integers to the integers such that, for all integers a, b, c with a + b + c = 0, f(a)^2 + f(b)^2 + f(c)^2 = 2 f(a) f(b) + 2 f(b) f(c) + 2 f(c) f(a).
problems.answer: f(x) = k x^2; f(x) = k for odd x and 0 for even x; f(x) = 0 for x = 0 mod 4, k for odd x, 4k for x = 2 mod 4 (k any integer)
problems.notes: the three families of solutions, written with k = f(1) (in every family f(1) = k; k = 0 is the zero function in all three); the test functions of the box include members of each family. imo_truth.py solves the equation on |x| <= 16 by exhaustive search and finds exactly these
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), (x1 + x2) + x3 = Z.zero -> (x0 x1 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x0 x2 ^ Npos (XO XH)) + x0 x3 ^ Npos (XO XH) = ((Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0 x1) * x0 x2 + (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0 x2) * x0 x3) + (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0 x3) * x0 x1) <-> (forall (x1 : Z), x0 x1 = x0 (Z.of_N (Npos XH)) * x1 ^ Npos (XO XH)) \/ ((forall (x1 : Z), (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) x1 -> x0 x1 = Z.zero) /\ (Not (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) x1) -> x0 x1 = x0 (Z.of_N (Npos XH)))) \/ (forall (x1 : Z), (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO XH)))) x1 -> x0 x1 = Z.zero) /\ ((Not (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) x1) -> x0 x1 = x0 (Z.of_N (Npos XH))) /\ (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) x1 /\ Not (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO XH)))) x1) -> x0 x1 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO XH))) * x0 (Z.of_N (Npos XH))))))

problems.name: imo2009_p5
problems.text: Determine all functions f from the positive integers to the positive integers such that, for all positive integers a and b, there is a non-degenerate triangle with sides of lengths a, f(b) and f(b + f(a) - 1).
problems.notes: f is a function on the integers whose values at the positive integers are positive; "non-degenerate triangle" means the three strict triangle inequalities. The answer is the identity (the published answer; the box only sees f(n) = n for n <= 8)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x1 -> Z.zero < x0 x1) -> (forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> Z.zero < x3 -> x2 < x0 x3 + x0 ((x3 + x0 x2) - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) /\ (x0 x3 < x2 + x0 ((x3 + x0 x2) - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) /\ x0 ((x3 + x0 x2) - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) < x2 + x0 x3)) <-> (forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> x0 x2 = x2)

problems.name: isl2006_n5
problems.text: Find all integer solutions of the equation (x^7 - 1)/(x - 1) = y^5 - 1.
problems.notes: there are no solutions; the quotient is written as the polynomial x^6 + x^5 + .. + 1 (which also covers x = 1, where it is 7 and 7 = y^5 - 1 has no integer solution either). The source label is from memory; imo_truth.py finds no solution with |x| <= 3000
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), (((((x0 ^ Npos (XO (XI XH)) + x0 ^ Npos (XI (XO XH))) + x0 ^ Npos (XO (XO XH))) + x0 ^ Npos (XI XH)) + x0 ^ Npos (XO XH)) + x0) + Z.of_N (Npos XH) = x1 ^ Npos (XI (XO XH)) - Z.of_N (Npos XH) -> False

problems.name: isl2007_n1
problems.text: Find all pairs (k, n) of positive integers such that 7^k - 3^n divides k^4 + n^2.
problems.notes: 7^k - 3^n is even and never zero, so "divides" is divisibility by a possibly negative integer
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI XH))) ^ x0 - Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) ^ x1) (Z.of_N x0 ^ Npos (XO (XO XH)) + Z.of_N x1 ^ Npos (XO XH)) <-> x0 = Npos (XO XH) /\ x1 = Npos (XO (XO XH))

problems.name: isl2007_n6
problems.text: Let k be a positive integer. Prove that the number (4k^2 - 1)^2 has a positive divisor of the form 8kn - 1 if and only if k is even.
problems.notes: n ranges over the positive integers (a divisor 8kn - 1 of (4k^2 - 1)^2 has n <= (4k^2 - 1)^2 / 8k, so for k <= 6 the witness window 450 is exhaustive). The source label is from memory (the problem is the key lemma of IMO 2007 P5, see imo2007_p5)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Ex Z (fun (x2 : Z) => Z.zero < x2 /\ Z.dvd ((Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO XH)))) * x0) * x2 - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) ((Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO XH))) * x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) ^ Npos (XO XH))) <-> Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) x0

problems.name: isl2008_n1
problems.text: Let n be a positive integer and p a prime number. Prove that if a, b, c are integers (not necessarily positive) satisfying a^n + p b = b^n + p c = c^n + p a, then a = b = c.
problems.notes: the chain of equalities a^n + p b = b^n + p c = c^n + p a is the two equations a^n + p b = b^n + p c and b^n + p c = c^n + p a
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), forall (x4 : Z), N0 < x0 -> Z.prime x1 -> x2 ^ x0 + x1 * x3 = x3 ^ x0 + x1 * x4 -> x3 ^ x0 + x1 * x4 = x4 ^ x0 + x1 * x2 -> x2 = x3 /\ x3 = x4

problems.name: isl2010_n2
problems.text: Find all pairs (m, n) of non-negative integers for which m^2 + 2 * 3^n = m (2^(n+1) - 1).
problems.notes: the equation is a quadratic in m, so for every n there are at most two values of m; imo_truth.py solves it for n < 60
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : N), Z.zero <= x0 -> x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) ^ x1 = x0 * (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ N.succ x1 - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) <-> x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI XH))) /\ x1 = Npos (XI XH) \/ (x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO XH)))) /\ x1 = Npos (XI XH) \/ (x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO XH)))) /\ x1 = Npos (XI (XO XH)) \/ x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI (XI (XO (XI XH)))))) /\ x1 = Npos (XI (XO XH))))

problems.name: isl2012_n2
problems.text: Find all triples (x, y, z) of positive integers with x <= y <= z and x^3 (y^3 + z^3) = 2012 (x y z + 2).
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> x0 <= x1 -> x1 <= x2 -> x0 ^ Npos (XI XH) * (x1 ^ Npos (XI XH) + x2 ^ Npos (XI XH)) = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))) * ((x0 * x1) * x2 + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) <-> x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) /\ (x1 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XO (XI (XI (XI (XI XH)))))))) /\ x2 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI (XI (XI XH)))))))))

problems.name: isl2015_n2
problems.text: Let a and b be positive integers such that a! + b! divides a! b!. Prove that 3a >= 2b + 2.
problems.notes: equality holds for a = b = 2
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> Z.dvd (Z.fact x0 + Z.fact x1) (Z.fact x0 * Z.fact x1) -> Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * Z.of_N x1 + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) <= Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) * Z.of_N x0

problems.name: isl2016_n4
problems.text: Let n, m, k and l be positive integers with n != 1 such that n^k + m n^l + 1 divides n^(k+l) - 1. Prove that m = 1 and l = 2k; or l divides k and m = (n^(k-l) - 1)/(n^l - 1).
problems.notes: the second case "l divides k and m = (n^(k-l) - 1)/(n^l - 1)" is written without subtraction in the exponent: k = l (i + 1) for some i >= 0 and m (n^l - 1) = n^(l i) - 1. n >= 2 stands for "n positive, n != 1"
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : N), forall (x3 : N), Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) <= x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> N0 < x2 -> N0 < x3 -> Z.dvd ((x0 ^ x2 + x1 * x0 ^ x3) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (x0 ^ (x2 + x3) - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) -> x1 = Z.one /\ x3 = N.double x2 \/ Ex N (fun (x9 : N) => x2 = x3 * N.succ x9 /\ x1 * (x0 ^ x3 - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) = x0 ^ (x3 * x9) - Z.of_N (Npos XH))

problems.name: isl2019_n2
problems.text: Find all triples (a, b, c) of positive integers such that a^3 + b^3 + c^3 = (a b c)^2.
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), forall (x2 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> N0 < x2 -> (Z.of_N x0 ^ Npos (XI XH) + Z.of_N x1 ^ Npos (XI XH)) + Z.of_N x2 ^ Npos (XI XH) = ((Z.of_N x0 * Z.of_N x1) * Z.of_N x2) ^ Npos (XO XH) <-> x0 = Npos XH /\ (x1 = Npos (XO XH) /\ x2 = Npos (XI XH)) \/ (x0 = Npos XH /\ (x1 = Npos (XI XH) /\ x2 = Npos (XO XH)) \/ (x0 = Npos (XO XH) /\ (x1 = Npos XH /\ x2 = Npos (XI XH)) \/ (x0 = Npos (XO XH) /\ (x1 = Npos (XI XH) /\ x2 = Npos XH) \/ (x0 = Npos (XI XH) /\ (x1 = Npos XH /\ x2 = Npos (XO XH)) \/ x0 = Npos (XI XH) /\ (x1 = Npos (XO XH) /\ x2 = Npos XH)))))

problems.name: isl2022_n1
problems.text: A number is called Norwegian if it has three distinct positive divisors whose sum is equal to 2022. Determine the smallest Norwegian number.
problems.notes: the statement says that every number with such three divisors is at least 1344, and that 1344 has them: 6 + 672 + 1344 = 2022
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> x1 < x2 -> x2 < x3 -> Z.dvd x1 x0 -> Z.dvd x2 x0 -> Z.dvd x3 x0 -> (x1 + x2) + x3 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI (XI (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))) -> Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH))))))))))) <= x0 /\ (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI XH))) < Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH)))))))))) /\ (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH)))))))))) < Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH))))))))))) /\ (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI XH)))) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH)))))))))))) /\ (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH))))))))))) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH)))))))))))) /\ (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH)))))))))))) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH)))))))))))) /\ (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI XH))) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH))))))))))) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI (XO (XI (XO XH))))))))))) = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI (XI (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI (XI (XI XH))))))))))))))))

problems.name: n5_n4_1_composite
problems.text: Prove that n^5 + n^4 + 1 is not a prime for any integer n > 1.
problems.notes: n^5 + n^4 + 1 = (n^2 + n + 1)(n^3 - n + 1), and both factors are larger than 1 once n > 1
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Z.of_N (Npos XH) < x0 -> Not (Z.prime ((x0 ^ Npos (XI (XO XH)) + x0 ^ Npos (XO (XO XH))) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)))

problems.name: composite_run
problems.text: Prove that for every natural number n there are n consecutive composite numbers: there is an integer a > 0 such that none of a + 1, a + 2, ..., a + n is a prime.
problems.notes: take a = (n + 1)! + 1: for 1 <= i <= n the number a + i = (n + 1)! + (i + 1) is divisible by i + 1, which lies between 2 and n + 1
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), Ex Z (fun (x1 : Z) => Z.zero < x1 /\ (forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> x2 <= Z.of_N x0 -> Not (Z.prime (x1 + x2))))

problems.name: n2_3n_5_not_121
problems.text: Prove that n^2 + 3n + 5 is never divisible by 121 (for an integer n).
problems.notes: 11 divides n^2 + 3n + 5 only for n = 4 (mod 11), and then n^2 + 3n + 5 = 33 (mod 121)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Not (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH)))))))) ((x0 * x0 + Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) * x0) + Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO XH)))))

problems.name: mersenne_base_2
problems.text: Let a > 1 and n >= 2 be integers. Prove that if a^n - 1 is a prime, then a = 2.  (Here n = m + 2 for a natural number m.)
problems.notes: a - 1 divides a^n - 1 and, for a >= 3, 1 < a - 1 < a^n - 1
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : N), Z.of_N (Npos XH) < x0 -> Z.prime (x0 ^ (x1 + Npos (XO XH)) - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) -> x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))

problems.name: mersenne_composite_exponent
problems.text: Let a > 1 be an integer and let the exponent n = (d + 2)(e + 2) be a product of two integers larger than 1. Prove that a^n - 1 is not a prime.
problems.notes: x = a^(d+2) satisfies x - 1 | x^(e+2) - 1 = a^n - 1, and 1 < x - 1 < a^n - 1
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : N), forall (x2 : N), Z.of_N (Npos XH) < x0 -> Not (Z.prime (x0 ^ ((x1 + Npos (XO XH)) * (x2 + Npos (XO XH))) - Z.of_N (Npos XH)))

problems.name: ineq_vasc
problems.text: Vasc's inequality: for all integers a, b, c:  3 (a^3 b + b^3 c + c^3 a) <= (a^2 + b^2 + c^2)^2.
problems.notes: twice the difference is the sum of the squares (a^2 - 2ab + bc - c^2 + ca)^2 + (b^2 - 2bc + ca - a^2 + ab)^2 + (c^2 - 2ca + ab - b^2 + bc)^2
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) * ((x0 ^ Npos (XI XH) * x1 + x1 ^ Npos (XI XH) * x2) + x2 ^ Npos (XI XH) * x0) <= ((x0 * x0 + x1 * x1) + x2 * x2) ^ Npos (XO XH)

problems.name: ineq_amgm_three
problems.text: For all non-negative integers a, b, c:  27 abc <= (a + b + c)^3  (the inequality between the arithmetic and the geometric mean of three numbers).
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero <= x0 -> Z.zero <= x1 -> Z.zero <= x2 -> ((Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XO (XI XH))))) * x0) * x1) * x2 <= ((x0 + x1) + x2) ^ Npos (XI XH)

problems.name: ineq_abc_2abc_1
problems.text: For all non-negative integers a, b, c:  a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 2abc + 1 >= 2 (ab + bc + ca).
problems.notes: two of a - 1, b - 1, c - 1 have the same sign, say (a - 1)(b - 1) >= 0; then the difference is (a - b)^2 + (c - 1)^2 + 2c (a - 1)(b - 1)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero <= x0 -> Z.zero <= x1 -> Z.zero <= x2 -> Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * ((x0 * x1 + x1 * x2) + x2 * x0) <= (((x0 * x0 + x1 * x1) + x2 * x2) + ((Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0) * x1) * x2) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)

problems.name: imo1983_p6_integer
problems.text: Let a, b and c be the lengths of the sides of a triangle (here: positive integers with a < b + c, b < c + a, c < a + b). Prove that  a^2 b (a - b) + b^2 c (b - c) + c^2 a (c - a) >= 0.  Determine when equality holds.
problems.answer: equality holds exactly when a = b = c
problems.notes: adapted: the sides are integers (the original has real sides). With x = b + c - a, y = c + a - b, z = a + b - c (all positive) one has 8 (a^2 b (a - b) + b^2 c (b - c) + c^2 a (c - a)) = zx (x - y)^2 + xy (y - z)^2 + yz (z - x)^2; equality forces x = y = z because the weights zx, xy, yz are at least 1

problems.name: fe_ring_hom
problems.text: Determine all functions f : Z -> Z such that f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) and f(x y) = f(x) f(y) for all integers x and y.
problems.answer: f = 0 or f(x) = x for all x
problems.notes: additivity gives f(n) = n f(1) for all integers n (induction in both directions), and f(1) = f(1)^2 leaves f(1) = 0 or 1
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), x0 (x1 + x2) = x0 x1 + x0 x2) -> (forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), x0 (x2 * x3) = x0 x2 * x0 x3) -> (forall (x3 : Z), x0 x3 = Z.zero) \/ (forall (x3 : Z), x0 x3 = x3)

problems.name: imo1977_p6
problems.text: Let f : N -> N be a function from the positive integers into the positive integers such that f(n + 1) > f(f(n)) for every positive integer n. Prove that f(n) = n for every positive integer n.
problems.notes: the function is formalised on the integers: only its values at positive integers are constrained. Induction on n shows that f(k) >= n for all k >= n; hence f(n) >= n and f(f(n)) >= f(n), so f is strictly increasing; then f(n) >= n + 1 would give f(f(n)) >= f(n + 1)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x1 -> Z.zero < x0 x1) -> (forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> x0 (x0 x2) < x0 (x2 + Z.of_N (Npos XH))) -> forall (x3 : Z), Z.zero < x3 -> x0 x3 = x3

problems.name: isl2005_n3
problems.text: Let a, b, c, d, e, f be positive integers and let S = a + b + c + d + e + f. Suppose that S divides abc + def and ab + bc + ca - de - ef - fd. Prove that S is composite.
problems.notes: S divides P(x) = (x + a)(x + b)(x + c) - (x - d)(x - e)(x - f) = S x^2 + (ab + bc + ca - de - ef - fd) x + (abc + def) for every integer x; at x = d the second product vanishes, so a prime S would divide (a + d)(b + d)(c + d) and hence one of the factors, but each of them lies strictly between 0 and S. "Composite" is "not a prime" (S >= 6). The source label (Mongolia, ISL 2005) is from the shortlist; the exact wording of the second divisibility condition is from memory (it is the one for which the polynomial identity above works)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), forall (x4 : Z), forall (x5 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> Z.zero < x2 -> Z.zero < x3 -> Z.zero < x4 -> Z.zero < x5 -> Z.dvd (((((x0 + x1) + x2) + x3) + x4) + x5) ((x0 * x1) * x2 + (x3 * x4) * x5) -> Z.dvd (((((x0 + x1) + x2) + x3) + x4) + x5) (((((x0 * x1 + x1 * x2) + x2 * x0) - x3 * x4) - x4 * x5) - x5 * x3) -> Not (Z.prime (((((x0 + x1) + x2) + x3) + x4) + x5))

problems.name: ineq_cyclic_27_4
problems.text: For all non-negative integers a, b, c:  27 (a^2 b + b^2 c + c^2 a + a b c) <= 4 (a + b + c)^3.
problems.notes: the expression is cyclic, so one may rotate the variables until y is the middle one of x, y, z; then 4 (x + y + z)^3 - 27 (x^2 y + y^2 z + z^2 x + x y z) = (x + z - 2y)^2 (4 (x + z) + y) + 27 z (x - y)(y - z), and both terms are non-negative. Equality holds for a = b = c and for (a, b, c) = (2, 1, 0) and its rotations
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero <= x0 -> Z.zero <= x1 -> Z.zero <= x2 -> Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XO (XI XH))))) * ((((x0 * x0) * x1 + (x1 * x1) * x2) + (x2 * x2) * x0) + (x0 * x1) * x2) <= Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO XH))) * ((x0 + x1) + x2) ^ Npos (XI XH)

problems.name: imo2016_p4a
problems.text: Let P(n) = n^2 + n + 1. A set of positive integers is called fragrant if it contains at least two elements and each of its elements has a prime factor in common with at least one of the other elements. Show that the set {P(196), P(197), P(198), P(199), P(200), P(201)} is fragrant. (This is the half of IMO 2016 P4 that shows that b = 6 is attained: the problem asks for the least positive integer b for which some non-negative integer a makes the set {P(a + 1), ..., P(a + b)} fragrant, and the answer is 6.)
problems.notes: the witness a = 195 (the set {P(196), .., P(201)}) is a variable with the hypothesis a = 195, so that the box sees the fragrant condition at other values of a as well; a = 196 is the next witness. Fragrant: each of the six values shares a prime factor with another one: P(196) = 3 * 61 * 211 and P(199) = 3 * 13267; P(197) = 19 * 2053 and P(201) = 19 * 2137; P(198) = 7 * 13 * 433 and P(200) = 7 * 5743
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI (XO (XO (XO (XO (XI XH)))))))) -> Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) <= Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI XH))) /\ (forall (x2 : Z), Z.one <= x2 -> x2 <= Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI XH))) -> Ex Z (fun (x5 : Z) => Z.one <= x5 /\ (x5 <= Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XI XH))) /\ (Not (x5 = x2) /\ Not (Z.coprime (((x0 + x2) * (x0 + x2) + (x0 + x2)) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (((x0 + x5) * (x0 + x5) + (x0 + x5)) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)))))))

problems.name: imo2016_p4b
problems.text: Let P(n) = n^2 + n + 1. A set of positive integers is called fragrant if it contains at least two elements and each of its elements has a prime factor in common with at least one of the other elements. Show that for every non-negative integer a and every b in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} the set {P(a + 1), ..., P(a + b)} is not fragrant. (This is the half of IMO 2016 P4 that shows that no b < 6 works: the problem asks for the least positive integer b for which some non-negative integer a makes the set {P(a + 1), ..., P(a + b)} fragrant, and the answer is 6.)
problems.notes: the fragrant condition is written with bounded quantifiers over the positions i, j in 1..b; the clause "at least two elements" is the conjunct 2 <= b. gcd(P(m), P(m + 1)) = 1, and gcd(P(m), P(m + d)) divides 7, 3, 19, 7 for d = 2, 3, 4, 5 (the case analysis of the official solution); imo_truth.py checks that no a < 10^6 works for b <= 5
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero <= x0 -> Z.one <= x1 -> x1 <= Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO XH))) -> Not (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) <= x1 /\ (forall (x5 : Z), Z.one <= x5 -> x5 <= x1 -> Ex Z (fun (x8 : Z) => Z.one <= x8 /\ (x8 <= x1 /\ (Not (x8 = x5) /\ Not (Z.coprime (((x0 + x5) * (x0 + x5) + (x0 + x5)) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (((x0 + x8) * (x0 + x8) + (x0 + x8)) + Z.of_N (Npos XH))))))))

problems.name: isl2000_n4
problems.text: Find all triples (a, m, n) of positive integers such that a^m + 1 divides (a + 1)^n.
problems.answer: a = 1 (any m, n); m = 1 (any a, n); and (a, m) = (2, 3) with n >= 2
problems.notes: "find all" as an equivalence with the answer: a = 1 (then a^m + 1 = 2 divides 2^n), m = 1 (a + 1 divides (a + 1)^n), or a = 2, m = 3 and n >= 2 (9 divides 3^n); there are no other triples
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : N), forall (x2 : N), Z.zero < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> N0 < x2 -> Z.dvd (x0 ^ x1 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) ((x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) ^ x2) <-> x0 = Z.one \/ (x1 = Npos XH \/ x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) /\ (x1 = Npos (XI XH) /\ Npos (XO XH) <= x2))

problems.name: isl2007_n2
problems.text: Let b and n be integers greater than 1. Suppose that for each integer k > 1 there exists an integer a_k such that b - a_k^n is divisible by k. Prove that b = A^n for some integer A.
problems.notes: adapted: "if b is an n-th power residue modulo every k > 1 then b is an n-th power" is written as an equivalence (the converse is trivial: for b = A^n take a_k = A). The condition is a statement about all k > 1; on the box it is tested for k <= 36, which refutes it for every b that is not an n-th power in the box (the first k for which b is not an n-th power residue is at most 31 for all b, n tested; imo_truth.py)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : N), Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) <= x0 -> Npos (XO XH) <= x1 -> (forall (x4 : Z), Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) <= x4 -> Ex Z (fun (x6 : Z) => Z.dvd x4 (x0 - x6 ^ x1))) <-> Ex Z (fun (x4 : Z) => x0 = x4 ^ x1)

problems.name: isl2012_n4b
problems.text: An integer a is called friendly if the equation (m^2 + n)(n^2 + m) = a (m - n)^3 has a solution over the positive integers. Decide whether a = 2 is friendly.
problems.notes: adapted: the answer of part (b) is "a = 2 is not friendly", written as the impossibility: no positive integers m, n satisfy (m^2 + n)(n^2 + m) = 2 (m - n)^3. Part (a) (at least 500 friendly integers up to 2012) is a statement about a count and is not in the bank. imo_truth.py finds no solution with m, n <= 2000
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> Not ((x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x1) * (x1 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x0) = Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * (x0 - x1) ^ Npos (XI XH))

problems.name: isl2012_n6
problems.text: Let x and y be positive integers. If x^(2^n) - 1 is divisible by 2^n y + 1 for every positive integer n, prove that x = 1.
problems.notes: adapted: the claim "the divisibility for every n >= 1 forces x = 1" is written as an equivalence (the converse is trivial: for x = 1 the number x^(2^n) - 1 is 0). The condition is a statement about all n >= 1; on the box it is tested for n <= 12, which refutes it for every x >= 2, y >= 1 in the box (the first failing n is at most 5 there)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> (forall (x4 : N), N0 < x4 -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x4 * x1 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (x0 ^ (Npos (XO XH) ^ x4) - Z.of_N (Npos XH))) <-> x0 = Z.one

problems.name: isl2013_n1
problems.text: Find all functions f from the positive integers to the positive integers such that m^2 + f(n) divides m f(m) + n for all positive integers m and n.
problems.notes: f is a function on the integers whose values at the positive integers are positive; the answer is the identity (the published answer; the box only sees f(n) = n for n <= 8)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x1 -> Z.zero < x0 x1) -> (forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> Z.zero < x3 -> Z.dvd (x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x0 x3) (x2 * x0 x2 + x3)) <-> (forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> x0 x2 = x2)

problems.name: isl2014_n2
problems.text: Determine all pairs (x, y) of positive integers such that the cube root of (7 x^2 - 13 x y + 7 y^2) equals |x - y| + 1.
problems.answer: (x, y) = (1, 1); (k^3 + k^2 - 2k - 1, k^3 + 2k^2 - k - 1) and the same pairs reversed, for k >= 2
problems.notes: the cube root is removed by cubing (the radicand 7x^2 - 13xy + 7y^2 is positive and |x - y| + 1 is positive, so the two equations are equivalent), and the absolute value by the two cases x >= y and x < y. Writing d = |x - y| and taking y = min(x, y) the equation becomes y^2 + d y + 7 d^2 = (d + 1)^3; imo_truth.py solves it exactly for d <= 2 * 10^6
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> x1 <= x0 /\ ((x0 - x1) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) ^ Npos (XI XH) = (Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI XH))) * x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) - (Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XI XH)))) * x0) * x1) + Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI XH))) * x1 ^ Npos (XO XH) \/ x0 < x1 /\ ((x1 - x0) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) ^ Npos (XI XH) = (Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI XH))) * x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) - (Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XI XH)))) * x0) * x1) + Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI XH))) * x1 ^ Npos (XO XH) <-> x0 = Z.one /\ x1 = Z.one \/ Ex Z (fun (x4 : Z) => Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) <= x4 /\ (x0 = ((x4 ^ Npos (XI XH) + x4 ^ Npos (XO XH)) - Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x4) - Z.of_N (Npos XH) /\ x1 = ((x4 ^ Npos (XI XH) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x4 ^ Npos (XO XH)) - x4) - Z.of_N (Npos XH) \/ x0 = ((x4 ^ Npos (XI XH) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x4 ^ Npos (XO XH)) - x4) - Z.of_N (Npos XH) /\ x1 = ((x4 ^ Npos (XI XH) + x4 ^ Npos (XO XH)) - Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x4) - Z.of_N (Npos XH)))

problems.name: isl2021_n1
problems.text: Determine all integers n >= 1 for which there exists a pair of positive integers (a, b) such that no cube of a prime divides a^2 + b + 3 and (a b + 3 b + 8) / (a^2 + b + 3) = n.
problems.notes: "find all" as an equivalence with the answer n = 2; the quotient is an integer exactly when n (a^2 + b + 3) = a b + 3 b + 8, and the witnesses are (a, b) = (2, 2) (9 and 18) and (4, 6). The condition "no cube of a prime divides a^2 + b + 3" is the statement that p^3 does not divide it for every prime p. imo_truth.py finds no other n with a < 400, b < 8000
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Ex Z (fun (x2 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x3 : Z) => Z.zero < x2 /\ (Z.zero < x3 /\ ((forall (x4 : Z), Z.prime x4 -> Not (Z.dvd (x4 ^ Npos (XI XH)) ((x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x3) + Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH))))) /\ ((x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x3) + Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH))) * x0 = (x2 * x3 + Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) * x3) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XO XH)))))))) <-> x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))

problems.name: apmo2019_p1
problems.text: Let Z+ be the set of positive integers. Determine all functions f from Z+ to Z+ such that a^2 + f(a) f(b) is divisible by f(a) + b for all positive integers a and b.
problems.notes: f is a function on the integers whose values at the positive integers are positive; the answer is the identity (the published answer; the box only sees f(n) = n for n <= 8)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x1 -> Z.zero < x0 x1) -> (forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> Z.zero < x3 -> Z.dvd (x0 x2 + x3) (x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x0 x2 * x0 x3)) <-> (forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero < x2 -> x0 x2 = x2)

problems.name: classic_ab_cd_sum
problems.text: If a, b, c, d are positive integers with a b = c d, then a + b + c + d is not a prime.
problems.source: classical (a classical olympiad exercise on composite numbers)
problems.notes: a + b + c + d >= 4; the classical proof: with g = gcd(a, c), a = g a1, c = g c1, a1 b = c1 d forces c1 | b, b = c1 t, d = a1 t, and the sum is (a1 + c1)(g + t)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), forall (x3 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> Z.zero < x2 -> Z.zero < x3 -> x0 * x1 = x2 * x3 -> Not (Z.prime (((x0 + x1) + x2) + x3))

problems.name: classic_odd_prime_pow_sum
problems.text: Let p be an odd prime and a, b integers such that p divides a^p + b^p. Prove that p^2 divides a^p + b^p.
problems.source: classical (a lemma of lifting the exponent)
problems.notes: a^p + b^p is congruent to a + b modulo p (Fermat), so p divides a + b, and then a^p + b^p = (a + b)(a^(p-1) - a^(p-2) b + .. + b^(p-1)) with the second factor congruent to p a^(p-1) modulo p. The claim is false for p = 2 (a = b = 1)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), Z.prime (Z.of_N x0) -> Not (x0 = Npos (XO XH)) -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N x0) (x1 ^ x0 + x2 ^ x0) -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N x0 ^ Npos (XO XH)) (x1 ^ x0 + x2 ^ x0)

problems.name: classic_descent_2xyz
problems.text: Find all integer solutions of the equation x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 2 x y z.
problems.notes: the sum of three squares on the left is even, so x, y, z are all even or exactly one is; modulo 4 the second case is impossible and the first gives (x/2, y/2, z/2) as a solution of x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 4 x y z, which descends the same way: every solution is divisible by every power of 2
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), (x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x1 ^ Npos (XO XH)) + x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) = ((Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0) * x1) * x2 -> x0 = Z.zero /\ (x1 = Z.zero /\ x2 = Z.zero)

problems.name: classic_two_coprime
problems.text: Every integer n >= 7 is the sum of two coprime integers, each greater than 1.
problems.notes: for odd n take 2 and n - 2; for n = 4k take 2k - 1 and 2k + 1; for n = 4k + 2 with k >= 2 take 2k - 1 and 2k + 3 (both odd, and their gcd divides their difference 4). The values 6 = 1 + 5 = 3 + 3 = 2 + 4 and 4 have no such decomposition, so 7 is where the claim starts (n = 5 = 2 + 3 works)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XI XH))) <= x0 -> Ex Z (fun (x2 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x3 : Z) => Z.one < x2 /\ (Z.one < x3 /\ (Z.coprime x2 x3 /\ x2 + x3 = x0))))

problems.name: classic_n4_4n
problems.text: Prove that n^4 + 4^n is not a prime for any positive integer n > 1.
problems.notes: formalised as: if n >= 1 and n^4 + 4^n is a prime then n = 1 (for n = 1 it is 5). For even n the number is even and larger than 2; for odd n = 2k + 1 it is n^4 + 4 (2^k)^4 = (n^2 + 2 n 2^k + 2 (2^k)^2)(n^2 - 2 n 2^k + 2 (2^k)^2), and the second factor is (n - 2^k)^2 + 2^(2k) > 1
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), N0 < x0 -> Z.prime (Z.of_N x0 ^ Npos (XO (XO XH)) + Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO XH))) ^ x0) -> x0 = Npos XH

problems.name: classic_fermat_little
problems.text: Fermat's little theorem: if p is a prime and a is an integer, then p divides a^p - a.
problems.notes: the prime is a natural number p (it is the exponent), a is any integer
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : Z), Z.prime (Z.of_N x0) -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N x0) (x1 ^ x0 - x1)

problems.name: classic_wilson
problems.text: Wilson's theorem: if p is a prime, then p divides (p - 1)! + 1.
problems.notes: the prime is p = q + 1 (q a natural number), so that (p - 1)! is q!
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), Z.prime (Z.of_N x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (Z.fact x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH))

problems.name: classic_wilson_converse
problems.text: If n > 1 is an integer such that n divides (n - 1)! + 1, then n is a prime.
problems.notes: n = q + 1 with q >= 1
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), N0 < x0 -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (Z.fact x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) -> Z.prime (Z.of_N x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH))

problems.name: classic_two_squares
problems.text: Every prime of the form 4k + 1 is a sum of two squares of integers (Fermat).
problems.notes: "of the form 4k + 1" is the hypothesis p = 4k + 1 on the integer k
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Z.prime x0 -> x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO XH))) * x1 + Z.of_N (Npos XH) -> Ex Z (fun (x4 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x5 : Z) => x0 = x4 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x5 ^ Npos (XO XH)))

problems.name: classic_four_squares
problems.text: Every non-negative integer is a sum of four squares of integers (Lagrange).
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Z.zero <= x0 -> Ex Z (fun (x2 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x3 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x4 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x5 : Z) => x0 = ((x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x3 ^ Npos (XO XH)) + x4 ^ Npos (XO XH)) + x5 ^ Npos (XO XH)))))

problems.name: classic_gcd_pow2
problems.text: If d is the greatest common divisor of the positive integers m and n, then 2^d - 1 is the greatest common divisor of 2^m - 1 and 2^n - 1.
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), forall (x2 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> Z.is_gcd (Z.of_N x0) (Z.of_N x1) (Z.of_N x2) -> Z.is_gcd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x0 - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x1 - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x2 - Z.of_N (Npos XH))

problems.name: classic_pythagorean
problems.text: Primitive Pythagorean triples: if a, b, c are positive integers with a^2 + b^2 = c^2, gcd(a, b) = 1 and b even, then there are coprime integers m > n > 0 with a = m^2 - n^2, b = 2 m n, c = m^2 + n^2.
problems.notes: "b even" is part of the hypothesis (in a primitive triple exactly one of a, b is even)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> Z.zero < x2 -> x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x1 ^ Npos (XO XH) = x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) -> Z.coprime x0 x1 -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) x1 -> Ex Z (fun (x9 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x10 : Z) => Z.zero < x10 /\ (x10 < x9 /\ (Z.coprime x9 x10 /\ (x0 = x9 ^ Npos (XO XH) - x10 ^ Npos (XO XH) /\ (x1 = (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x9) * x10 /\ x2 = x9 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x10 ^ Npos (XO XH)))))))

problems.name: classic_2n_not_div
problems.text: Prove that no integer n > 1 divides 2^n - 1.
problems.notes: the proof looks at the least prime divisor p of n: the order of 2 modulo p divides n and p - 1, hence is 1
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), Npos XH < x0 -> Not (Z.dvd (Z.of_N x0) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x0 - Z.of_N (Npos XH)))

problems.name: classic_xy_yx
problems.text: Find all pairs of positive integers (x, y) with x^y = y^x.
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> Z.of_N x0 ^ x1 = Z.of_N x1 ^ x0 <-> x0 = x1 \/ (x0 = Npos (XO XH) /\ x1 = Npos (XO (XO XH)) \/ x0 = Npos (XO (XO XH)) /\ x1 = Npos (XO XH))

problems.name: classic_pq_qp
problems.text: Find all primes p and q such that p^q + q^p is a prime.
problems.notes: if p, q are both odd the sum is even; if p = 2 and q > 3 then 2^q + q^2 is a multiple of 3
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), Z.prime (Z.of_N x0) -> Z.prime (Z.of_N x1) -> Z.prime (Z.of_N x0 ^ x1 + Z.of_N x1 ^ x0) <-> x0 = Npos (XO XH) /\ x1 = Npos (XI XH) \/ x0 = Npos (XI XH) /\ x1 = Npos (XO XH)

problems.name: classic_fact_composite
problems.text: If n > 4 is a composite integer, then n divides (n - 1)!.
problems.notes: n = q + 1, so that (n - 1)! is q!; composite means "not prime" for n > 4
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), Npos (XI XH) < x0 -> Not (Z.prime (Z.of_N x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH))) -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (Z.fact x0)

problems.name: classic_bertrand
problems.text: Bertrand's postulate: for every positive integer n there is a prime p with n < p <= 2n.
problems.notes: checked here for n <= 40 and by imo_truth.py for n < 100000
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Ex Z (fun (x2 : Z) => Z.prime x2 /\ (x0 < x2 /\ x2 <= Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0))

problems.name: classic_primes_3mod4
problems.text: There are infinitely many primes of the form 4k + 3: for every n there is a prime p > n with p = 4k + 3.
problems.notes: the proof: if p_1 .. p_r were all of them, 4 p_1 .. p_r - 1 has a prime factor of the form 4k + 3
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), Z.zero <= x0 -> Ex Z (fun (x2 : Z) => Ex Z (fun (x3 : Z) => Z.prime x2 /\ (x0 < x2 /\ x2 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO XH))) * x3 + Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)))))

problems.name: classic_pyth_60
problems.text: If a, b, c are integers with a^2 + b^2 = c^2, then 60 divides abc.
problems.source: classical (the product of a Pythagorean triple)
problems.notes: the argument looks at the three primes: 3 divides one of a, b; 4 one of a, b (or both are even); 5 one of a, b, c
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x1 ^ Npos (XO XH) = x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) -> Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO (XO (XI (XI (XI XH))))))) ((x0 * x1) * x2)

problems.name: classic_consecutive_product
problems.text: The product of n consecutive non-negative integers m (m + 1) .. (m + n - 1) is divisible by n!.
problems.source: classical (n! divides a product of n consecutive integers)
problems.notes: the product is Z.prod over i < n of m + i (the empty product is 1)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : N), Z.zero <= x0 -> Z.dvd (Z.fact x1) (Z.prod (fun (x3 : Z) => x0 + x3) x1)

problems.name: classic_fermat_coprime
problems.text: The Fermat numbers F_k = 2^(2^k) + 1 are pairwise coprime.
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), Not (x0 = x1) -> Z.coprime (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ (Npos (XO XH) ^ x0) + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ (Npos (XO XH) ^ x1) + Z.of_N (Npos XH))

problems.name: classic_3x_2y
problems.text: Find all pairs of positive integers (x, y) with 3^x - 2^y = 1.
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) ^ x0 - Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x1 = Z.one <-> x0 = Npos XH /\ x1 = Npos XH \/ x0 = Npos (XO XH) /\ x1 = Npos (XI XH)

problems.name: classic_2x1_3y
problems.text: Find all pairs of positive integers (x, y) with 2^x + 1 = 3^y.
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH) = Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) ^ x1 <-> x0 = Npos XH /\ x1 = Npos XH \/ x0 = Npos (XI XH) /\ x1 = Npos (XO XH)

problems.name: classic_2x_3y_square
problems.text: Find all non-negative integers x, y, z with 2^x + 3^y = z^2.
problems.notes: z is taken non-negative (z and -z give the same equation)
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), forall (x2 : N), Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) ^ x0 + Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) ^ x1 = Z.of_N x2 ^ Npos (XO XH) <-> x0 = N0 /\ (x1 = Npos XH /\ x2 = Npos (XO XH)) \/ (x0 = Npos (XI XH) /\ (x1 = N0 /\ x2 = Npos (XI XH)) \/ x0 = Npos (XO (XO XH)) /\ (x1 = Npos (XO XH) /\ x2 = Npos (XI (XO XH))))

problems.name: classic_fact_product_sum
problems.text: Find all positive integers a, b, c with a! b! = a! + b! + c!.
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), forall (x2 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> N0 < x2 -> Z.fact x0 * Z.fact x1 = (Z.fact x0 + Z.fact x1) + Z.fact x2 <-> x0 = Npos (XI XH) /\ (x1 = Npos (XI XH) /\ x2 = Npos (XO (XO XH)))

problems.name: classic_fact_sum_fact
problems.text: Find all positive integers a, b, c with a! + b! = c!.
problems.statement: forall (x0 : N), forall (x1 : N), forall (x2 : N), N0 < x0 -> N0 < x1 -> N0 < x2 -> Z.fact x0 + Z.fact x1 = Z.fact x2 <-> x0 = Npos XH /\ (x1 = Npos XH /\ x2 = Npos (XO XH))

problems.name: classic_x2_y3_1
problems.text: Find all pairs of positive integers (x, y) with x^2 = y^3 + 1.
problems.notes: y^3 = (x - 1)(x + 1): the factors are coprime or have gcd 2
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> x0 ^ Npos (XO XH) = x1 ^ Npos (XI XH) + Z.of_N (Npos XH) <-> x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) /\ x1 = Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))

problems.name: classic_y2_x3_2
problems.text: Find all pairs of positive integers (x, y) with y^2 = x^3 - 2.
problems.notes: the standard proof factorises y^2 + 2 in Z[sqrt(-2)], a unique factorisation domain: this is far outside what the agent can do and is in the bank as a statement to be recognised, not as a goal
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero < x0 -> Z.zero < x1 -> x1 ^ Npos (XO XH) = x0 ^ Npos (XI XH) - Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) <-> x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH)) /\ x1 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO XH)))

problems.name: classic_2p1_cube
problems.text: Find all primes p for which 2p + 1 is a perfect cube of an integer.
problems.notes: the cube is n^3 for an integer n: 2p + 1 = n^3 means p = (n - 1)(n^2 + n + 1)/2
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z), forall (x1 : Z), Z.prime x0 -> Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH)) * x0 + Z.of_N (Npos XH) = x1 ^ Npos (XI XH) <-> x0 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI (XO (XI XH)))) /\ x1 = Z.of_N (Npos (XI XH))

problems.name: classic_fe_n2_1
problems.text: Find all functions f from the integers to the integers such that f(m + n) + f(mn - 1) = f(m) f(n) + 2 for all integers m and n.
problems.source: classical functional equation over the integers
problems.notes: m = 0 gives f(0) = 1 and f(-1) = 2 (no constant solves the equation); then m = 1 and m = -1 determine f from f(1) = t, and t = 2 is the only value that works; imo_truth.py solves it exactly on |n| <= 12
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), x0 (x1 + x2) + x0 (x1 * x2 - Z.of_N (Npos XH)) = x0 x1 * x0 x2 + Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) <-> (forall (x1 : Z), x0 x1 = x1 ^ Npos (XO XH) + Z.of_N (Npos XH))

problems.name: classic_fe_sum_prod
problems.text: Find all functions f from the integers to the integers such that f(x + y) + f(x y) = f(x) f(y) + 1 for all integers x and y.
problems.source: classical functional equation over the integers
problems.answer: f(n) = 1; f(n) = n + 1; f(n) = 1 for even n and 0 for odd n
problems.notes: f(0) = 1 follows from x = 0, then x = 1 gives f(y + 1) = (f(1) - 1) f(y) + 1, so f is determined by f(1) = t, and t = 0, 1, 2 are the only values that work
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), forall (x2 : Z), x0 (x1 + x2) + x0 (x1 * x2) = x0 x1 * x0 x2 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) <-> (forall (x1 : Z), x0 x1 = Z.one) \/ ((forall (x1 : Z), x0 x1 = x1 + Z.of_N (Npos XH)) \/ (forall (x1 : Z), (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) x1 -> x0 x1 = Z.one) /\ (Not (Z.dvd (Z.of_N (Npos (XO XH))) x1) -> x0 x1 = Z.zero)))

problems.name: classic_fe_sum_squares
problems.text: Let f be a function from the non-negative integers to the non-negative integers with f(1) > 0 and f(m^2 + n^2) = f(m)^2 + f(n)^2 for all m, n. Prove that f(n) = n for all n.
problems.source: classical functional equation over the integers
problems.notes: f is a function on the integers whose values at the non-negative integers are non-negative and satisfy the equation there; f(0) = 0, f(1) = 1, f(2) = 2, f(4) = 4, f(5) = 5 and then every f(n) follows from identities like 3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2 + 0^2, in general from (2k+1)^2 + (k-2)^2 = (2k-1)^2 + (k+2)^2
problems.statement: forall (x0 : Z -> Z), (forall (x1 : Z), Z.zero <= x1 -> Z.zero <= x0 x1) -> Z.zero < x0 Z.one -> (forall (x3 : Z), forall (x4 : Z), Z.zero <= x3 -> Z.zero <= x4 -> x0 (x3 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x4 ^ Npos (XO XH)) = x0 x3 ^ Npos (XO XH) + x0 x4 ^ Npos (XO XH)) -> forall (x4 : Z), Z.zero <= x4 -> x0 x4 = x4
